messages:
maria: Hey, getting a spike of dropped packets and connection resets for GPU training pods in west2 since the Cilium upgrade last night. Several jobs stalled with high tail latency.
kevin: saw alerts too. p99 token latency up ~4-5x on inter-pod traffic across nodes. Any recent network rollouts? :thinking:
sasha: Cilium 1.18 rotated through the cluster at 02:30 UTC (DS rollout). I can confirm CNI version bumped from 1.17.4 -> 1.18.0 on all gpu nodepools.
maria: logs show lots of `connection reset by peer` in trainer containers and the k8s kubelet logs show `networking: write failed` for some pod IPs.
olivia: ops-bot surfaced a cluster alert: `east-west-packet-loss > 15%` for the past 90m on west2-gpu pool. Repro locally with simple iperf between two gpu nodes.
kevin: quick iperf3 between two problematic nodes:
```
Client connecting to 10.244.12.45, TCP port 5201
[ ID] Interval           Transfer     Bandwidth       Retr  Cwnd
[  4]   0.00-10.00  sec  8.35 GBytes  7.17 Gbits/sec  3129             (loss visible)
```
kevin: tcpdump on node shows lots of fragmented geneve packets and ICMP "need to frag" messages. Also seeing GSO/GRO warnings in dmesg.
sasha: ddump from node kernel:
```
[  +0.000000] IPv4: martian source 10.244.12.45 from 10.244.11.23, dev cilium_host
[  +0.000000] skb_do_segment: skb_gso_segment: GSO type 0x1 not supported
```
maria: that GSO/GRO failure matches old cilium bug patterns when tunnel offloads interacting with NICs that do strict MTU checks. We have 9001 MTU on the nodes and geneve encaps adds ~50B overhead.
olivia: reproduced with `ping -s 8700` across nodes — lots of fragmentation and 20-30% packet loss.
kevin: note: some of our GPU nodes use RDMA NICs and require certain offloads disabled for RoCE; Cilium's tunnel mode might be enabling/assuming different offload behavior.
sasha: I dug through the 1.18 changelog — they changed default fragment handling and tunneled checksum/GSO passthrough logic. There are a couple of upstream reports that 1.18 interacts poorly with Mellanox/ConnectX firmware versions.
maria: immediate impact: ~120 training pods impacted, several experiments restarted; scheduling churn is causing extra costs. Estimate about ~$3-5k in lost GPU time so far.
olivia: can we rollback the DaemonSet to 1.17 from the rollout? deploy-bot do we have the previous image in our registry?
deploy-bot: previous images available: gcr.redwood/cilium:1.17.4 and gcr.redwood/cilium:1.18.0. Rolling rollback requires cordoning + draining GPU nodes to avoid killing pods — will take ~2-3 hours of maintenance for full pool.
kevin: short-term mitigation: switch Cilium to policy-only mode or disable encapsulation to force host-networking for pod-to-pod on same node? Not ideal for cross-node traffic.
sasha: We can patch the Cilium configmap to set tunnel: disabled but that requires kernel support for direct routing and will break cross-subnet routing — risky.
maria: For now, can we do a canary rollback: pick 2 GPU nodes, roll them to 1.17 and run iperf/real training job to validate? If green, we schedule full rollback during off-peak window tonight.
olivia: +1 to canary. I'll pick two nodes in west2-gpu-pool-a and coordinate with SRE. Need approval from infra lead first.
kevin: also propose a short-term iptables rule to clamp MSS for tunnel paths to avoid fragmentation: set TCPMSS clamping on vxlan/geneve interfaces. Not perfect (UDP/rdma still affected) but may reduce TCP resets.
sasha: a grep of Cilium logs shows repeated cilium-agent warnings about failed offload: `failed to enable GRO on tunnel-device: operation not supported` — suggests driver/firmware mismatch.
maria: action items:
- sasha: run canary rollback on nodes gpu-045/gpu-046 and validate (target in next 30m)
- kevin: prepare iptables MSS clamp recipe and a short doc for ops
- olivia: schedule maintenance window if canary successful, notify customers for west2 impact
- sasha: open upstream issue with kernel/dpdk/cilium logs and attach tcpdumps

sasha: starting canary rollback now: `kubectl set image ds/cilium cilium-agent=gcr.redwood/cilium:1.17.4 -n kube-system --record`
sasha: cordoning gpu-045
sasha: draining with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` (we accept some pod restarts for canary)
kevin: MSS clamp rule I'm testing:
```
iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```
kevin: initial quick test between canary nodes: iperf3 now shows stable throughput, retransmits < 100 over 10s.
maria: great. Keep monitoring. If canary holds 10-15m with no training job failures, greenlight full pool rollback.
olivia: sending ETA to product/support: "Investigating networking regression in west2 affecting GPU jobs. Temporary canary rollback underway; may affect scheduling for ~2-3 hours."
sasha: canary finished: cilium pods on gpu-045/gpu-046 are running 1.17.4 and we see no geneve fragmentation in tcpdump; training job resumed normally.
maria: approve full rollback during maintenance window 23:00-02:00 UTC. olivia will post incident/update.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0457. Priority: P2. Assigned: eng-infra.
kevin: follow-up: schedule firmware checks for Mellanox NICs on west2. We should also pin cilium image until upstream fixes fragment handling.
maria: also open a cost tracking ticket for lost GPU compute and include in postmortem.
olivia: noted. I'll draft the postmortem and communications.
sasha: opened upstream bug + PR request with kernel logs and pcap attached: https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/12045
maria: thanks everyone. If anything else pops, ping here. :thumbsup:
